title: Deep phenotyping of fusion oncoprotein-driven pediatric cancer metastasis with single-cell proteomics
text:
When cancers lack immunocompetent mouse models, we have limited access to evaluate
the effect of tumor-immune cell interactions on metastatic capacity. To address this gap, we propose introduction
of integrated engineered tumor microenvironments with multiplexed single-cell electrophoretic analysis capable
of quantifying protein complex expression, cell structure and motility. We will test specific hypotheses on the
metastatic phenotypic heterogeneity of Ewing sarcoma cells in the presence of distinct immune cell populations
in the tumor microenvironment.

title: Highspeed Image Sensor and Microscopy Methods for Resolving Millisecond Scale Neural Dynamics in Freely Moving Mice and Zebrafish
text: Neural signaling is the basis of communication and computation in neural circuits. This project focuses on developing new image sensors for direct optical readout of neural signals, including calcium and voltage signals, from a large number of neurons across different animal species during naturalistic behaviors. This technology will provide critical insights into neural circuit computation and how disease states affect these circuits within a local region and across larger brain areas.

title: Prostate Cancer Biomarker and Imaging Validation Alliance: Emory University, University of Alabama Birmingham, and University of Texas Southwestern
text:
Our center uniquely combines patient and specimen resources from a breadth of health care settings in/near
Atlanta (Grady Memorial Hospital in Atlanta, the Atlanta VAMC in Decatur, St. Joseph's Hospital in Sandy
Springs, and Emory University Hospital in Atlanta) together with the University of Alabama in Birmingham and
the University of Texas -Southwestern Medical Center in Dallas and partners with laboratories from throughout
the U.S. to improve detection of prostate cancer. We also seek to determine which of these cancers should be
treated and which ones can be safely managed without treatment.

title: Technology development for high-resolution biological imaging and structural dynamics
text:
Technology development for high-resolution biological imaging and structural dynamics
This proposal aims to develop innovative technologies for high-resolution, dynamic imaging of biological
molecules to advance the field of structural biology. Understanding the structure and dynamics of large
biological molecules and their interactions at room temperature with near atomic resolution is a key goal in
structural biology. These advancements have the potential to significantly enhance our understanding of
biomolecular function, identify new drug targets, and improve human health through better treatments and
therapies.

title: Oncogenic Chromatin Remodeling and Anticancer Mechanisms
text:
mTOR is a central controller of cancer growth and an anticancer target. This application will test the central
hypothesis that aberrant mTOR signaling promotes oncogenic chromatin remodeling through degradation of the
tumor suppressor ARID1A, which is important for cancer development and response to mTOR-targeted cancer
therapies.

title: Core 2: Bioinformatics and Biostatistics
text:
The Bioinformatics and Biostatistics core is a comprehensive resource for advanced adaptive clinical trial design and
multi-omic biomarker data analysis and synthesis within the I-SPY2.2 Program Project. We will work closely with each
of the project teams to provide project-specific analytical support, as well as facilitate cross-project analyses, to ensure
that analyses conducted are consistent across projects and apply the highest standards of statistical rigor.

title: Genetically Modified Mouse Resources Core
text: Type 2 immune responses protect against helminth infections but also drive allergic diseases and asthma that affect over 2 billion people worldwide. Understanding how these responses are regulated across different tissues is essential for developing targeted therapies that enhance protective immunity while suppressing pathological inflammation. The Genetically Modified Mouse Resources Core (GMMRC) will provide standardized mouse models essential for investigating tissue-specific mechanisms of Type 2 immunity across gut, skin, and lung environments. The broad objective of the GMMRC is to support the program project grant by serving as a centralized resource that eliminates experimental variability, enhances reproducibility, and increases productivity by completing three tasks. First, the core will maintain and distribute a comprehensive colony of knockout and knockin mouse strains, consolidating strains currently maintained redundantly across individual laboratories and realizing economies of scale. Second, the core will ensure all strains are protist-free and maintained on >99% C57BL/6 genetic backgrounds, eliminating two major confounding variables that significantly impact Type 2 immune responses. Third, the core will generate or import additional mouse strains required for hypothesis testing, utilizing CRISPR/Cas9 genome editing to rapidly create new models in response to emerging discoveries. The GMMRC will directly support four research projects investigating Type 2 immunity mechanisms, enabling cross-tissue comparisons using identical genetic tools and standardized experimental conditions. By maintaining common reporter strains and tissue-specific targeting tools, the core will facilitate identification of both conserved and tissue-specific immune mechanisms. Additionally, the services provided by the core will reduce the burden of colony management, allowing program researchers to focus on experiments. Lastly, the standardized mouse models and elimination of confounding variables will accelerate translation of basic discoveries into clinical applications for allergic diseases, asthma, and helminth infections, ultimately contributing to therapeutic approaches that can enhance human health by modulating tissue-specific immune responses.

title: Discerning mechanisms of semaphorin 7A-mediated tumor progression via immunoevasion
text:
We have shown that SEMA7A promotes multiple aspects of breast cancer progression, including proliferation,
survival, invasion, and immune evasion. The F99 portion of this proposal (Aim 1) aims to investigate SEMA7A-
mediated alterations to TAMs and T cells in the TME responsible for suppressing anti-tumor immunity and if
targeting SEMA7A directly can impede tumor growth and immunoevasion. The K00 aspect of this application
(Aim 2) proposes to identify novel mechanisms of immunoevasion in renal cell carcinoma and pancreatic
ductal carcinoma, which may reveal novel targets for treatment to prevent metastases and prolong patient
survival.

title: Leveraging deep learning to classify sitting posture and measure sedentary patterns from accelerometer data in diverse cohorts
text:
Adults in the US spend over 50% of their waking day being sedentary, i.e., in a sitting or lying
posture. Being sedentary is known to confer higher risk of diabetes and heart disease, yet
sedentary time has increased greatly the 1960s given the rise of technologies that have
automated jobs and incorporated screens into occupational and leisure activities. In this
project, we will use advanced computation techniques to accurately quantify an individual’s
sedentary behavior patterns with the ultimate goal of developing guidelines for reducing
sedentary behavior and promoting healthy living, wellbeing and longevity.

title: Integrated super-resolution CMR-deep learning to deconvolute passive and active causes of impaired relaxation
text:
Heart failure in the left ventricle occurs when the heart cannot provide sufficient blood flow to the body. About
half of heart failures happen when the left ventricle cannot properly relax. Despite the common understanding
that poor relaxation is caused by changes in active characteristics of the left ventricle, our findings suggest that
changes in passive properties of the left ventricle tissue play a key role in poor relaxation. In this application, we
propose to separate the contributions of passive and active changes to poor relaxation and determine if restoring
passive properties improves the left ventricle relaxation.

title: Epigenetic regulation of natural killer cell memory
text:
Immunological memory can come in two formats: (1) the well-studied classic antigen-specific responses of the
adaptive immune arm, and (2) trained immunity, an emerging but still-developing concept of a nonspecific
immune memory primarily mediated by innate cells. This proposal seeks to understand the epigenetic
foundations that differentially or commonly define trained immunity and antigen-specific memory by studying a
unique case study whereby natural killer (NK) cells, a part of the innate arm, can acquire both types of memory
features. Defining the molecular mechanisms by which NK cells acquire heritable and durable effector and
memory potential will unveil novel strategies to improve NK cell-based therapies.

title: Multi-Modal, Multi-Depth, High Resolution Micro-Endoscope (M3D-HRME) for early cancer diagnostics
text:
Proposal will carry out feasibility studies to develop a new class of optical micro-endoscopic
devices for early stage, cancer detection. Micro-endoscopic devices will be fabricated using
high precision 3D printing.

title: Robust and Interpretable Multi-modal AI/ML for Precision Medicine
text:
Multi-modal integration in biomedical research offers great opportunities to advance precision medicine by combining
multi-omics, medical imaging, and clinical narrative data. This project seeks to develop robust and interpretable
AI/ML models for the integration of incomplete multi-modal biomedical modalities. The proposed
methods will mitigate the challenges of data heterogeneity and incomplete or missing data, which are expected
to increase the power and rigor of integrative multi-modal analysis of biomedical data, and provide deeper insights
into complex diseases such as cancer and Alzheimer’s disease.

title: Mayo Clinic Center for Clinical Proteomics
text:
The major goal of the Mayo Clinic Center for Clinical Proteomics is to apply the most advanced proteomics and
genomics technologies for characterizing multiple myeloma cell lines and patient-derived cells to identify markers
of immunomodulatory drug resistance and to validate them using clinical trial samples. Our highly innovative and
interdisciplinary team with expertise in multiple myeloma research and treatment, proteomics and genomics
technologies/instrumentation, targeted assay development, clinical chemistry and bioinformatics will maximize
the chances of successful clinical translation of protein markers of drug resistance in multiple myeloma.

title: Nonhuman Primate Reagent Resource
text:
The Nonhuman Primate Reagent Resource (NHPRR) develops, produces, qualifies, and distributes biologic
reagents that enable rigorous, reproducible research in nonhuman primates. These specialized reagents make
it possible to study immune mechanisms and to evaluate immunization, immunotherapies, and transplantation
strategies in models that closely reflect human biology. By sustaining and advancing this national resource and
its experienced team, this renewal ensures that the NHPRR continues to strengthen the quality and impact of
preclinical research nationwide, accelerating progress toward improved treatments and prevention of human
disease.

title: A digital intervention to decrease self-stigma among pregnant and postpartum women with opioid use disorder
text:
The opioid epidemic has resulted in increasing overdose deaths and widespread detrimental health
consequences throughout the United States, particularly among vulnerable populations, including pregnant
and postpartum women (PPW) with opioid use disorder (OUD). Self-stigma is exceptionally high among PPW
with OUD and may prevent their treatment initiation and engagement, leading to adverse health outcomes for
both mother and baby. The work in this grant will enable us to iteratively refine and implement a digital
therapeutics tool, Enhearten, designed to decrease self-stigma and improve treatment adherence and progress
toward recovery among PPW with OUD.

title: Identification and characterization of novel genes causative for primary ciliary dyskinesia
text:
Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia (PCD) is a complex genetic disease that can lead to severe and recurring
respiratory infections. We have developed the tools to quantifiably distinguish key cellular features of
PCD and will characterize known and potential PCD causing genes. Additionally, we will perform a
tiered CRISPR/Cas9 screen to identify and characterize novel PCD genes.

title: Mechanisms of Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitor-induced Sinoatrial Node Dysfunction
text:
Sinoatrial node (SAN) dysfunction is a critical adverse effect of Tyrosine Kinase inhibitors (TKI) used in the
treatment of advanced non-small cell lung cancer. This study will investigate the molecular mechanisms
underlying TKI-induced SAN dysfunction. The proposed research is expected to provide new fundamental
insights into SAN biology and cardio-oncology, opening potential avenues for the development of novel
therapeutic strategies to mitigate cardiotoxic effects in cancer patients.

title: Uncovering isoform-specific functions of RNA-binding protein Bruno1 in Drosophila muscle development
text:
An estimated 1 in 8,000 people are affected by the muscle disorder myotonic dystrophy, which is
caused by a genetic defect that leads to muscle malfunction and mis-regulation of RNA-binding
proteins including CELF1. This proposal utilizes the powerful genetic model organism Drosophila
melanogaster to elucidate foundational mechanisms of CELF homolog Bruno1 isoform-specific
function in RNA regulation during muscle development, including analysis of cellular and
behavioural phenotypes, identification of transcriptome-wide regulatory signatures, and
biochemical evaluation of RNA target binding affinity and preference. Considering the high level
of conservation from flies to humans in muscle structure and function, our results will advance
understanding of CELF factor regulatory dynamics in myogenesis and have the potential to
provide human disease-relevant insight into isoform-specific function of CELF family proteins.

title: Development of mHealth-Supported Skills Training for Alcohol and Related Suicidality (mSTARS): Emotion Regulation Skills Training to Enhance Acute Psychiatric Care and Recovery
text:
Recently discharged psychiatric inpatients who misuse alcohol are at high risk for suicide. The proposed
project involves the development of a novel intervention that would enhance care for these individuals by
pairing inpatient-based emotion regulation skills training with a mobile health application that extends this
treatment into the post-discharge period. Through acquisition and eventual utilization of emotion regulation
skills to replace maladaptive, stress-induced emotion-driven behaviors (e.g., heavy drinking, suicide attempts),
this approach could reduce post-discharge risk for a suicide crisis and costly rehospitalization.
